experiment: UC1 STT (Whisper size) selection + end-to-end error propagation
hardware: Apple M1 Pro, 16 GB; faster-whisper (CTranslate2) CPU int8; LLM qwen2.5:7b on Metal
testset: data/testset/audio_labels.json (60 clips x quiet/noisy; macOS say TTS, AWGN @ SNR 10 dB)
caveats: Synthetic TTS is 'easy' for ASR (clean voice); noise is white-Gaussian, a stand-in for cafe/babble. WER/CER are therefore optimistic; the relative ranking across sizes/engines/conditions is the usable signal. CER/WER are punctuation- and space-insensitive (content only) so an engine is not penalised for its punctuation style.

stt_size_sweep.metric_note: EN WER, JA CER (char-level), both punctuation/space-insensitive; RTF = asr_time / audio_seconds (>1 = slower than real time)
stt_size_sweep.rationale: Best Japanese CER (1.8%) and comfortably real-time (RTF 0.57). Medium is slower than real time (1.96x) with no Japanese gain; tiny/base trade too much JA accuracy for speed. Confirms the configured default empirically.

stt_quiet_vs_noisy.note: At SNR 10 dB, JA CER roughly triples (1.8->5.3%) and EN WER roughly doubles (4.6->8.6%) — still usable.

stt_engine_comparison.finding: Engine-level test (parity with the LLM study): the Japanese-specialised Kotoba-Whisper did NOT beat general Whisper small here — higher CER and ~2x slower. A punctuation artifact was found and removed first (Kotoba emits no 、。); the residual gap is NOT orthographic: Kotoba OMITS the customer-name phrase (Xと申します / 名前はX) in 10/36 clips. Dropping a required field is disqualifying for this task, and clean TTS also favours the general model. Caveat: Kotoba targets spontaneous speech, so a test on real Japanese phone audio is future work.

findings: ASR error propagation hits NAME hardest: 100% (text) -> 90% (quiet) -> 75% (noisy). Cause: Japanese homophone surnames mis-transcribed (佐藤->砂糖, 山本->山元, 渡辺->ワタナベ).
DATE is LLM-limited, not ASR-limited: ~50-55% across text/quiet/noisy. Cause: relative-date/weekday reasoning, independent of transcription quality.
time and party_size are robust to ASR error (>=95% everywhere).
end_to_end.implication: Two independent bottlenecks need two different fixes: NAME -> ASR/biasing or confirmation step; DATE -> deterministic date resolver (hybrid). The 85% target is met on text, just missed end-to-end on clean audio (84.6%).
